name: AI incidents & governance
summary: US charges three over a $129m deepfake executive fraud; no AI attack on critical infrastructure found
state: US prosecutors charged three men accused of using AI-generated voices and images of chief executives and lawyers to take more than $129m from businesses, including hospital systems in Missouri and California and a Rhode Island bank (ITPro, 6 Nov). No AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure or AI-attributed mass harm was found as of 13 Nov, so the level stays Watch.
for_you: Finance and accounts staff are the main targets of deepfake executive fraud, which tends to rely on urgent, confidential payment requests. The NCSC and Action Fraud publish guidance on verifying such requests through a separate channel.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant AI misuse incident — $129m deepfake executive fraud charged (6 Nov); no AI attack on critical infrastructure

sources.title: ITPro — Three charged after impersonating CEOs and attorneys in $129 million deepfake fraud scheme

why: Powerful AI systems are being deployed faster than safeguards; serious incidents or governance breakdowns carry systemic risk.
drivers: Model releases, misuse incidents, regulation, compute controls, deepfakes in elections.

rubric.alert: AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure, or AI-attributed mass harm event.
rubric.watch: A significant AI misuse incident, major deepfake disruption, or regulatory confrontation.
rubric.normal: No serious AI-attributed harm events or governance shocks this week.
